# Beta catalogue maintenance

Unidentified add-on bundles are held outside the prepared catalogue until their individual contents can be established. Retain their original stable IDs and source evidence in the research backlog; restore an entry only after listing its actual contents. A game name or a generic “DLC bundle” filename is not sufficient evidence. Package identity checks do not establish installation compatibility.

## Current catalogue

Catalogue revision 99 (18 November 2026) adds the first PS4 game updates: **565 updates with 652 download options (470 Vikingfile, 182 AkiraBox) for 410 PS4 games**, 297 of them backports for older firmware. A file is taken when SuperPSX's index lists it as an update, its version matches the label and is above 1.00, and Vikingfile or AkiraBox confirms its name and size. A file whose name doesn't say Update or Patch is left out when it is within 1% of the size of Orbit's game PKG for that title, or when Orbit has no plain game PKG to compare it with: such a file is more likely the full game at a newer version. They are carried in the v8 feed's separate `updates` array (see [Game updates](#game-updates)) and change no game, add-on or download counts.

Catalogue revision 97 (17 November 2026) adds Metacritic scores and HowLongToBeat playtimes for 211 more PS4 games, mostly the 324 added in revision 95, which came after the last insights pass: **543 PS4 games now have a score and 932 a playtime** (revision 96: 433 and 742). It changes only `insights` and is published in `catalogue-v8.enc` alone, the only feed PS4 apps read. 49 games stay without the new values because the snapshot's play styles are out of order or its edition is ambiguous. Evidence: `.state/insights-review/`.

Catalogue revision 95 contains **2,644 games** (1,210 PS5 and 1,434 PS4), **5,486 game download options**, and **631 add-ons with 633 options across 197 base games**. The PS4 app shows **1,434 games and 1,551 download options**, plus **533 add-ons with 535 options across 120 base games**. The approved v3–v8 feeds remain in use; v6 retains its limited compatibility catalogue with 3,850 options at revision 83. Orbit for PS5 1.8.5 packages bundle revision 87 (2,261 games and 5,084 options); the published PS4 0.0.1 and 0.0.2 packages bundle revision 94. Compatible apps receive the newer catalogue through refresh.

Revision 95 imports 324 PS4 games and 324 download options from the four PS4 focus checkpoints: 81 Vikingfile options and 243 AkiraBox options. Sayonara Wild Hearts remains held because its source-labelled game file is consistent with a small update rather than the separately indexed full package, and its alternate public Archive route requires sign-in. The 40 PS4 New on Orbit picks come from this batch and follow recorded PlayStation Store global player-rating counts, highest first. Those counts can span editions and platforms; they are a popularity indicator, not Orbit download counts. Existing game metadata, options and add-ons are retained, apart from replacing the previous PS4 discovery ranks. Import, popularity, native-reader and publication evidence is retained in `.state/ps4-catalogue-publication-2026-11-15/`. Bounded headers, archive directories and public file listings do not establish payload integrity, signing or installation compatibility.

Revisions 93–94 add 59 games (five PS5 and 54 PS4), 78 download options and 620 classifications for existing options. The classifications comprise 227 inspected Vikingfile archives and 393 AkiraBox mirrors matched by game, title ID, filename, compression and exact byte size. Matching metadata supports reuse of the archive classification; it does not prove identical payloads. The 73 held archive inspections and 131 unqualified PS4 candidates remain outside this import. Existing add-on data and the 40-tile display limit are unchanged. Revision 94 restores the owner’s second featured pick and shifts the other selections down. Import, popularity and publication evidence is saved in `.state/local-catalogue-release-2026-11-05/`. Bounded archive checks do not establish full payload integrity, package signing, installation or firmware compatibility.

### PlayStation exclusives

The **PlayStation exclusive** tag means games officially available only on PlayStation platforms. Games with official PC, Xbox or Nintendo versions are excluded, including older editions of a game subsequently ported or remade for those platforms. Unofficial ports and emulation do not count. Editions on PS4 and PS5 share the classification when appropriate. Tags are reviewed per game, not inferred from its publisher. Platform evidence and review dates are retained in `tagEvidence` in the private game metadata and are not published in the catalogue feeds. Recheck the tag when a new official port is announced or released. Browse exposes the tag in all three clients.

### Add-on records and compatibility

`catalog/addons.json` holds stable add-on IDs, base-game associations, platform, type, display metadata, contents, requirements and per-add-on release options. `tools/addons.py` compiles the separate collection and validates associations, content identities and options. Game records remain in `catalog/games.json` and `catalog/releases.json`; an add-on must not be imported as a base game.

The v8 feed contains separate game, add-on and game-update collections. v7 and older feeds continue to carry only compatible base-game data. Add-on counts do not change game totals, featured rows or base-game download status. Queue snapshots retain the chosen add-on identity and requirements across catalogue refreshes. Seeing a matching base-game title ID in Library does not establish DLC compatibility or installation.

The base-game exclusions below still apply to base-game imports. DLC uses the add-on schema, which accepts identified activation packages and bundles as well as individual content. Game updates have their own collection (below); dead links, ambiguous associations and unsupported providers remain outside the add-on import. Read [Add-ons](addons.md) for the user flow and [installation](package-installation.md) for explicit bundle selection.

### Game updates

`catalog/updates.json` holds PS4 game updates (patches): one record per title ID, version and firmware build, with `id` (`update-cusa01154-1-16-505`), the base game's `gameId`, a `titleId` that one of that game's PS4 options uses, `version` (above 1.00), `requiredFirmware` (the oldest firmware the file runs on, from the source label: "BackPort 6.72/7.xx/9.00" is 6.72), `backport` and one or more provider `releases`. `tools/updates.py` compiles them into the v8 feed's separate `updates` array: each option gets the base game's display fields and its own source evidence, checked as base-game options are. Games, add-ons and updates together stay within the console's 8,192 options. Update rows never count as games, and older apps ignore the array. Only `updates.enc` goes into source bundles; the plain lists stay out.

An update file is imported only when the provider's own filename names the title ID, says Update, and gives the same version and firmware as the source label. Files that modify or merge content, name another region's title ID or give no firmware are held. A newer version that runs on the same or older firmware replaces older ones, since the console never picks those.

## Refresh and build

```sh
npm run catalog:metadata
npm run catalog:verify
npm run catalog:build
npm run test:catalog
npm run build
```

To refresh one item, append `-- --only <game-id>` to `catalog:metadata`, or `-- --only <release-id>` to `catalog:verify`. Network requests are serial, with at least eight seconds between requests to the same host. HTTP 403, 429 or 503 ends the run and reports `Retry-After`; do not rotate domains or bypass a challenge. Completed items are saved individually. Normal builds make no metadata, artwork or game requests.

Review fetched titles against the curated game identity before committing. Publisher pages can change their default edition. `metadataOverrides` records an explicit exception with its reason and evidence URL. Publisher release dates are regional storefront dates, not firmware compatibility or download-version information. Descriptions/taglines are curated separately from publisher marketing copy.

## Import researched single-file sources

`tools/import_catalog.py` stages entries from the research JSON into a separate directory. Pass `--catalogue`, `--pippo`, one or more `--pegasus` snapshots and `--output`. It preserves existing game/release IDs, matches artwork by PS5 title ID, and keeps unsupported Vikingfile landing pages in research candidates only. Compressed archives, multipart sets and PKGs are excluded. `tools/import_viking.py` stages reviewed single-file Vikingfile pages for the PS5 browser flow. It reconciles game identities, preserves existing records, uses title-ID-matched external artwork, and distinguishes public file metadata from direct-download range evidence. Pass the selected candidates, recorded metadata checks, source snapshots and an output directory; it never fetches, publishes or fabricates direct routes.

Run `.venv/bin/python tools/verify_import.py <staging-directory>` before promoting the staged `games.json` and `releases.json`. When exact metadata and matching HEAD evidence already exist, the verifier records their original timestamps and performs a fresh 16-byte range check. Missing evidence triggers all three probes. Check `verification-status.json` for completion with no failures, then regenerate the embedded snapshot. Interrupted runs preserve successful checks.

Unknown publisher, release date, genre and description fields remain null. Add a reviewed PlayStation `metadataUrl` to enrich them with the common metadata fetcher. Discover’s Latest releases row uses up to 20 games with verified dates, newest first, excluding future dates. New on Orbit appears before Latest releases. Games with an optional `newOnOrbitRank` (an integer from 1 to 100) lead the row in ascending rank order. The remaining places, up to 40 games total, are filled with the newest catalogue additions and displayed by game release date, newest first, with undated games last. Ranked games are included only once. New links for existing games do not change their catalogue addition date. All games uses a grid ordered by the largest available download option first. Browse and Discover’s All games grid scroll continuously; the browser adds 96 cards at a time as the end comes into view.

A game's optional `tags` list adds it to Browse's Tags filter, in the browser, TV app and Orbit Zero. Supported tags are `exclusive`, `local-coop`, `split-screen`, `open-world`, `story-driven`, `soulslike`, `psvr-supported` and `psvr2-supported`. Add them to the game in `games.json`; the build copies them to each of that edition’s options. Selected tags match **any** selected tag; platform, source, format and other filters narrow those results further. Local co-op means cooperative play on one console, while Split-screen also includes competitive play. PSVR supported and PSVR2 supported include both required and optional VR modes. Check the actual platform edition: PS4 editions do not inherit PSVR2 support from shared store pages. Required headsets and mode restrictions are explained in the game description. Classification evidence and dates remain in private `tagEvidence` metadata. A missing tag means the game has not been classified, not necessarily that it lacks the feature. `tools/catalog.py` accepts only tags in its `KNOWN_TAGS`; add a new one there only after the apps have its label (`TAGS` in `src/browse.ts` and Orbit Zero's `src/catalogue-filter.mjs`, `kTags` in the TV app's `model.cpp`) and its translations. The apps accept up to eight well-formed tags (lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, up to 32 characters) and ignore ones they have no label for, so a newer catalogue's tags never break an older build. The Tags filter only appears once a game has a labelled tag.

## Artwork

The original 147-game catalogue uses `cdn.prosperopatches.com` first. The expanded catalogue also uses title-ID-matched external URLs from its recorded source snapshots. Previous Sony URLs are retained in `coverFallback` and `heroFallback` where available. For covers, the browser tries the backup after the primary image fails, then uses the local Orbit mark if both fail. Browser 0.7.0 and later retry a distinct `heroFallback` when the primary wide banner fails or decodes as a square image. The ambient cover stays visible until a wide image is ready and remains if both candidates fail. Released browser 0.6.1 returns to the ambient cover without this wide-banner retry. Of those original 147 games, 97 retain their original Sony backups; the other 50 have no previously verified Sony URLs. New entries retain alternate source artwork URLs where available, without claiming they were image-probed. Run `.venv/bin/python tools/artwork.py --apply` to replace remaining primary artwork from other hosts, then compile or prepare the catalogue feed. The tool reads each exact title page, verifies its title ID and the CDN image signature, and checkpoints results in the ignored `.state/artwork-prospero.json`. Requests are serial, three seconds apart per host (`--interval`, at least one; the other catalogue tools keep eight), and stop on challenges or rate limits. Unavailable matches are reported and left unchanged. Publisher metadata refreshes preserve these reviewed primary and backup choices.

Banners come from the same CDN. Next to each title's icon, the Prosperopatches folder holds the game's PS5 background, `pic0.webp` (normally 1920 x 1080). `tools/artwork.py --banners` probes it for every game whose cover is a title-ID-matched icon: a 32-byte range request must return a WebP whose header gives its size, and only a wide image (at least 1.4 times as wide as tall, the storefronts' own banner rule) is accepted. `--apply` stores the result in the game's `banner` record (provider, title ID, URL, measured size, check time) and makes it the `hero` with the `wide` layout. The publisher's banner, where one exists, stays in `heroFallback`. Results are checkpointed in the ignored `.state/artwork-banners.json`; checked folders are not probed again. Metadata refreshes and later cover moves keep a verified banner, and the compiler rejects a banner whose URL, title ID or size does not match its game. The catalogue has verified 1920 x 1080 CDN banners for 575 of 581 games. Six reviewed external replacements now fill the remaining wide backgrounds; four JPEG/PNG cover replacements remove the remaining primary AVIF covers. These artwork changes and the metadata pass below are published as catalogue revision 13. Previously the primary artwork used the ambient layout; some games could still show a wide publisher image through `heroFallback` when that host was reachable.

For titles absent from Prosperopatches, `externalArtwork` retains the matched game/title IDs and each asset's publisher page, URL, format, dimensions and check time. Microids, Mandragora's official site, THQ Nordic and publisher Steam artwork supply five titles. Sonic's unofficial-port entry uses a 960 x 540 screenshot from Sega's original PS3/Xbox 360 game page as illustrative artwork, not a claim about the PS5 port; the unofficial label and its unset release metadata remain. All previous Sony backups are unchanged. The compiler rejects mismatched identities, provider hosts, Steam app IDs, unsupported formats and non-wide backgrounds; metadata refresh reapplies reviewed choices. Temporary image downloads were inspected outside the repositories; only URLs and evidence are retained.

Only external HTTPS URLs are stored. The fetcher checks image headers or a bounded 32-byte image signature without storing artwork assets. Cards use cover art; a game's detail page and focused Discover card use its wide background when available. Otherwise the cover becomes a blurred ambient background. Cards load lazily, and only the focused game's large background is mounted. Cover fallback handling is shared by Discover, Browse, game details, Downloads and Library. Image requests omit the referrer.

There is no artwork upload, image proxy, account key or live metadata dependency. Game images are not embedded in the ELF, source archive or either repository. The browser may use its normal HTTP cache. External artwork availability and host URL changes remain outside Orbit's control.

## What a verified source means

Included Archive.org options were checked against the item's exact file listing, a successful HEAD response with matching total size, and a 206 response for a 16-byte range with a matching `Content-Range`. No full game downloads are performed by this tool. Verification is point-in-time availability evidence, not proof of authenticity, installability, entitlement, DLC contents or console compatibility. Source-reported hashes are retained as evidence; they are not promoted to trusted checksums.

Single `.ffpfsc`, `.exfat` and FPKG `.pkg` files are eligible. FPKG imports retain the upstream format label for the exact file link separately from live filename/size checks; that label is not a binary or console test. Orbit saves the package file to the selected destination; installation is an explicit **Install on PS5** action in 1.5.0 (see [installation](package-installation.md)). `.ffpkg` disk images, archive collections, generic HTML pages, multipart sets and compressed archives do not qualify for this import. An exact Vikingfile file page may be listed for browser-assisted delivery when its public metadata confirms the selected filename and byte size. It cannot be queued as a direct download. Changing an option's URL, filename or size invalidates its recorded verification until checked again. The compiler rejects duplicate identities/URLs, missing core metadata, local artwork paths, malformed dates, unsupported formats and fields that exceed console buffers.

Vikingfile direct options use a reviewed `https://vikingfile.com/d/<id>/<encoded-filename>` route. Their evidence records a successful one-byte GET, exact range total and matching filename. The verifier and downloader use GET because a storage signature may not authorize HEAD. exFAT, FFPFSC and FPKG `.pkg` names are supported, including percent-encoded spaces. Signed storage URLs are never saved to the catalogue or queue.

Browser-only options use the same exact `/f/<id>` file page in `url` and `browserUrl`. Their `verification.kind` is `file-metadata`, including the public check-file endpoint, file hash, exact filename/size and original check date. Compiled rows retain `sourceVerification: file-metadata`; this does not claim that a download range or full transfer was checked. The API exposes `browserAvailable: true` and `directAvailable: false`. Orbit opens the page only on user request, checks the captured filename-bound `/d/` route with a one-byte request, and queues it only after validation. Direct queue requests for file pages are rejected.

The 2026-10-04 expansion adds 429 games and 511 options (447 options for new games and 64 for existing games). Of those, 487 reuse recorded exact public metadata checks from October 2-4; the remaining 24 received fresh checks for missing exact sizes. No new full-file downloads were performed. The staged report is retained locally under `.state/viking-expansion/`; it is not release content. New covers are title-ID-matched external URLs from the saved source catalogues, with alternate URLs retained where available. Publisher dates, genre and descriptions remain unset when not independently sourced.

A `/d/` route can become unavailable while its original file page remains available. Retain the original public source link in `importEvidence`; resolve and verify a fresh route through the normal provider flow. Do not assume `/d/` IDs are permanent. Full transfers and console acceptance of the expanded options remain unverified. Sonic Unleashed Recompiled is explicitly labelled as an unofficial port. Nioh 3's `.7z` archive remains excluded.

## 1fichier and DataNodes evidence

1fichier is deferred since Orbit for PS5 1.3.5 because the physical PS5 browser could not load its provider page over SSL. The 499 researched options and nine games left without another active source are saved privately for a later release; none are in the current release feed.

1fichier options retain their permanent public file page in both `url` and `browserUrl`. A public metadata check must confirm the exact filename and byte size. `file-metadata` evidence does not claim that a full download or extraction has been tested. Regional editions map to the existing game when identity matches; multipart sets, demos, utilities and unclear standalone fixes stay out of the game catalogue. Compressed contents use the rules below. Provider browser and TorBox flows remain implemented for future acceptance testing.

DataNodes public file pages expose rounded sizes. Those values are not exact byte sizes and must not be used for `sizeBytes`. The generated file response can supply its exact size through headers or a one-byte range request after the normal provider steps. The bulk runner stops when provider verification is required and records those candidates as pending, without downloading the game or treating them as import-ready.

## Console acceptance

The desktop source probes and browser tests do not mark `consoleVerified` true. Verify the new payload on the console, including download, pause/resume, recovery and startup lifecycle, before changing release gates. The diagnostic entry remains separate from the game catalogue.

## Publish catalogue changes without an ELF update

This working tree fetches `catalogue-v8.enc` on startup and every six hours, with capacity for 8,192 download options in a feed up to 16 MiB. Earlier compatible builds retain `catalogue-v6.enc`, supporting archives, AkiraBox and DataNodes. Version 1.1.0 keeps `catalogue-v5.enc`, which leaves out compressed options and those new providers. Older FPKG-capable builds retain the PS5-only `catalogue-v4.enc`; Orbit 0.8.0 uses `catalogue-v3.enc`, containing PS5 FFPFSC and exFAT options. Update Orbit Store and its native app once to add new capabilities; later compatible additions arrive through the catalogue feed. **App settings → Game catalogue → Refresh catalogue** checks immediately, subject to the shared cooldown. Both interfaces use the ELF backend; the native FFPKG bundles that same ELF.

From the source checkout:

1. Edit `catalog/games.json` and `catalog/releases.json`, preserving stable identities and verification evidence.
2. Verify changed options with `npm run catalog:verify -- --only <release-id>`.
3. Run `npm run catalog:publish -- --public-repo <public-worktree>`.
4. Review `catalogue-v8.enc` (games, add-ons and updates), `catalogue-v7.enc` (base games), the compatible `catalogue-v6.enc`, the archive-free `catalogue-v5.enc`, the PS5-only `catalogue-v4.enc` and `catalogue-v3.enc`, source snapshots and revision. Commit corresponding changes together when ready. This command does not commit, push, build an ELF or fetch URLs.

The publisher retains the highest revision across feeds and increases it for content changes. It validates inputs before writing and reuses unchanged snapshot bytes. The bundled `catalog/catalog.enc` and v8 public feed carry the same game, add-on and update collections. v7 contains compatible base games only. The v6 feed excludes 1fichier; v5 and older also exclude compressed options, AkiraBox and DataNodes. One unsupported row rejects a client's whole catalogue. The publisher checks the older feeds against their 4,096-option and 8 MiB limits before writing any files. If a proposed older feed exceeds either limit, it preserves that generation's previous authenticated, compatible, within-limit feed byte-for-byte, including its revision. A missing or invalid previous feed stops publication before writing. Current and other compatible feeds still update, and repeating the publication does not increase the revision. v4 and v3 also exclude PS4 editions; v3 also excludes FPKG. Publish v8 alongside apps that support Add-ons; retain compatible v7 base-game data for earlier readers. Users of a preserved feed need an app update for newer catalogue additions. Pre-0.8.0 apps retain their bundled or saved catalogue. Historical commits and release assets remain unchanged.

## Compressed options

An option can be a single ZIP, 7z or RAR archive that Orbit extracts after downloading. `compression` is `zip`, `7z` or `rar`, and the filename must have that extension. The provider evidence verifies the archive's identity, exact filename and compressed `sizeBytes`.

For a reviewed archive, `format` describes its contents (`exFAT`, `FFPFSC`, `FPKG`, `PKG` or `Game folder`) and `extractedBytes` is the measured total of its regular files. Exclude Mac clutter (`__MACOSX/`, `.DS_Store`, `._*`). Extraction refuses a result whose total differs from that declared size.

When contents have not been inspected before import, use `archiveContents: "unverified"`, `format: "Unknown"` and omit `extractedBytes`. This requires the same confirmed game identity, complete game metadata and working provider-file evidence as other imports. It must not invent the internal format or unpacked size. The compiler rejects a mixture of these fields and a declared extracted size. Separate backports, DLC-only items, multipart filenames and ambiguous game identities remain excluded from base-game imports. DLC belongs in the separate add-on collection described above.

All clients display the actual packaging label (ZIP, RAR or 7z) and compressed size. Browse includes compressed downloads by default; choose ZIP, RAR or 7z in the Format filter to narrow the list. The download sheet explains that Orbit checks the archive and available space before extracting it. The internal schema value `Unknown` is not a product label.

LZ4 game assets use the optional v8 `contentFormat: "LZ4"` subtype. This is separate from the outer `compression` archive. Only PS5 base-game archives can carry it. A source classification needs an explicit LZ4 source record and matching provider-file evidence; filenames alone are not enough. Keep `format: "Unknown"` and `archiveContents: "unverified"` until the archive contents are inspected, or use `format: "Game folder"` and measured `extractedBytes` after inspection. Never infer an extracted size from a source's estimate. The 1.7.5 clients display and filter the option as LZ4 (for example `RAR · LZ4`); earlier v8 clients retain their existing archive handling. Revision 62 identifies 49 such options across 48 PS5 games, including 28 previously catalogued options and 21 newly added options. Packaging filters still match these options. LZ4 asset packs are preserved inside the extracted game folder, not recursively decompressed by Orbit. The label does not confirm runtime or console compatibility. No new feed generation is required.

After a download completes, Store and Zero inspect the archive listing without writing extracted files. They reject unsafe paths, links, special files, duplicate or conflicting names, multipart volumes and invalid sizes. All regular files and folders are extracted, apart from Mac filesystem clutter; notes, multiple packages and unrecognised layouts are allowed on either platform. Recognising a package/exFAT/FFPFSC file or game folder supplies a label, not an extraction requirement or proof of console compatibility. Other layouts retain `Unknown` internally. Measured bytes and detected format are saved on the job; its original catalogue identity stays unchanged. Extraction proceeds only after the required free-space reservation succeeds. On a password, archive or space error, the downloaded archive is retained for recovery.

An optional `archivePassword` contains 1–128 UTF-8 bytes without control characters. Both apps also try `DLPSGAME.COM`, `[DLPSGAME.COM]`, `SuperPSX`, `www.DLPSGAME.COM`, `downloadgameps3.com`, `hako` and `pippo`. A custom per-download password can be entered from Downloads. Missing password evidence never means an archive is password-free.

On the PS5, files are extracted in a private `.orbit-extract-<job>` staging folder in `homebrew`, then moved into place without overwriting existing names. **Storage → Delete archives after extracting** is on by default. **Storage → Extract archives after downloading** (on by default) can be turned off: compressed downloads added afterwards finish as the archive under its own name and need room only for the archive. Orbit Zero extracts on the computer with its included 7-Zip, validates the output and transfers the files to the PS5. A compressed download needs room only for the archive when it is queued and while it downloads. Just before unpacking, Orbit checks for room for the extracted files (the measured size after inspection when the catalogue has none) beside what other downloads still need; without it, the download waits paused with the archive kept until space is freed and it is resumed. Only one console extraction runs at a time.

## PS4 editions

The feed carries PS4 and PS5 games. The PS4 app shows only PS4 games and add-ons, with matching counts and no platform filter. Details show each game's own release date when known. Users install completed packages explicitly through **Install on PS4**; downloading a package never installs it automatically.

Each game and option has `platform: ps4` or `ps5`, backed by an exact CUSA or PPSA title ID. PS4 and PS5 editions use separate game IDs even when their names match. Favourites, artwork and library matching follow that identity. PS4 options accept `.pkg` files, either raw or inside a supported single archive: `FPKG` when the source explicitly identifies that subtype, otherwise `PKG`. Multipart sets remain excluded. Recorded source notes appear beside the chosen download option.

Keep research outside the application catalogue. Preview imports with `.venv/bin/python tools/import_ps4.py <research.json>`; add `--apply` only after reviewing the result. Every imported game needs matching file evidence, an original description and one-liner, a verified PS4 release date, publisher, genre, a checked cover and a measured wide banner. Incomplete candidates stay in research. Artwork URLs retain their source and edition provenance; images are not bundled. Archive.org options need a bounded successful range response; Vikingfile browser options need exact public file metadata and are validated again after the user's browser step. Region tags from filenames remain evidence only until a matching official content ID supports them. Prospero-only artwork and region lookups skip CUSA records. Generic publisher refreshes preserve these separately reviewed PS4 metadata records rather than replacing them with a combined PS4/PS5 store page.

Validated catalogue snapshots are cached atomically. Invalid data falls back to the bundled catalogue. Queued downloads retain their selected files across catalogue changes, and cache migration preserves queue and pairing state. TorBox queue compatibility is described in [TorBox downloads](debrid.md).

Release sources include the `.enc` snapshot inputs and every reader, required decoding input and build tool. `catalog:check` and `embed.py` build directly from these files using a host C compiler and OpenSSL. Run `catalog:build` after editing catalogue data. Release packaging rejects stale snapshot inputs.

## Discovery metadata

`games.json` includes `addedAt`, the first catalogue-addition timestamp. Existing games use their first source-catalogue commit timestamps; new games receive a timestamp on first publishing when none is set. Preserve it on metadata corrections and alternate source additions. The publisher writes this field back to the source snapshot. Browse defaults to the independently verified release date for each platform, newest first, with undated games last and titles breaking ties. Catalogue addition dates do not affect Browse ordering. At the 0.5.0 release, 27 of 581 games have recorded dates. Remaining metadata enrichment is deferred until after release and can ship through the catalogue feeds without another ELF.

Catalogue revision 9 adds 138 reviewed PS5 release dates, bringing coverage to 165 of 581 games; 416 remain undated. Publisher and genre fields are filled where the same official Store result supports them. Each changed record retains its source URL, PS5 platform match, retrieval timestamp and date basis. US Store dates are used for the matched edition, including early-access dates where listed; they are not necessarily worldwide launch dates. Ape Escape and Ape Academy 2 use their original US Classics launch announcements instead of the later Store SKU reissue dates, with explicit overrides to preserve those corrections. Conflicting title/edition matches remain unset. Artwork, fallbacks and download identities are unchanged.

Catalogue revision 10 adds 40 reviewed PS5 release dates and publisher records, plus 39 genre records. That revision brought coverage to 205 of 581 games, with 376 dates remaining. The batch checked 50 additional titles and resolved two earlier title-punctuation matches. Ambiguous edition matches and Toy Story 2's later Store reissue date remain pending. The same regional date basis applies; artwork, fallbacks, download links and game/option identities are unchanged.

Catalogue revision 13 adds 303 reviewed dates after searching all 376 previously undated titles. Coverage is 508 of 581 games; 73 dates remain unresolved. It also adds 302 publisher fields, 296 genre fields and five original short descriptions. Regional Store dates retain their locale and date basis. Matching PS5 product/concept pages take precedence over PS4 SKUs; demo URLs and different editions are excluded. Jumping Flash!, Syphon Filter 2 and Killzone: Liberation use their original US Classics availability announcements instead of the later Store reissue dates. Every changed record retains its source URL and review evidence. Existing dates, artwork, backup URLs, download links and identities are preserved.

## Regions

A PS5 title ID does not name its region; its content ID does: the first letter is the region (`U` USA, `E` Europe, `J` Japan, `H` Asia), followed by `P`, or `B` for newer publisher IDs (`UP`, `EB`, `HB`). `.venv/bin/python tools/regions.py --apply` records each option's `region` from two sources: the title ID's public Prosperopatches page, and the Sony store product link the game's metadata came from when that product is for the same title ID. A page counts only when it is for the same title ID, its content ID contains that title ID, and its stated region agrees with the prefix. Each source is kept in `regionEvidence`; where both exist they must agree, and anything else leaves the option without a region. Source-list region tags are not used. Pages are requested one at a time, three seconds apart, and the run stops on a challenge or rate limit. Results are checkpointed in the ignored `.state/regions.json`, so checked title IDs are not requested again. The page's update list (versions, required firmware) is behind a reCAPTCHA and is not read. The compiler checks every recorded region against its sources and keeps the evidence out of the feeds. The browser and native Browse interfaces use this field in the Region filter; older apps ignore it. Region, source, format and size must match the same download option. Unknown regions remain visible under All regions and have a separate Unknown region choice.

Browse combines source, format and size filters against the same download option. Size sorting uses the smallest option that matches those filters. Favourites are game IDs saved on the console, shared with paired clients, and unaffected by source filtering.


The catalogue contains 515 browser-enabled options: four previously range-checked options retain their direct shortcut, and 511 new file-page options require browser verification. Only the three remaining direct-only Vikingfile options omit the browser action. The previously tested handoff does not establish console compatibility or full-transfer completion for every new entry.

## Reviews and estimated playtimes

Games can include optional `insights.metacritic` and `insights.howLongToBeat` records in the existing v8 catalogue. They do not change game/download identities or base-game counts. Clients display the score, platform, playtime styles and service attribution. Missing records remain unknown; they are never filled with zero or guessed. Scores and playtime filters exclude unknown values only while that filter is selected, and sorting places unknown values last in either direction.

The curator tools use published offline snapshots, not per-game requests from Orbit clients:

```sh
python3 tools/enrich_game_insights.py --hltb-zip /path/to/hltb.zip --metacritic-zip /path/to/metacritic.zip --platform-score-zip /path/to/platform-scores.zip --output .state/insights-review
python3 tools/game_insights.py .state/insights-review/insights-import.json
# After reviewing the matches:
python3 tools/game_insights.py .state/insights-review/insights-import.json --apply
python3 tools/catalog.py build
python3 tools/game_insights.py --missing .state/insights-review/missing.json
```

Run this process after importing new games as well as when refreshing older metadata. Exact normalized titles, edition names and supported platforms must match uniquely. Headline Metacritic values are accepted only for single-platform entries; the other score snapshot supplies explicitly platform-specific PS4/PS5 rows. Playtimes use documented per-style averages with at least three submissions. Ambiguous editions and inconsistent playtime rows remain in the review report. Never silently substitute another platform, edition or service. Newer games absent from the snapshots stay in the missing-data queue until checked records are available. A curator can also supply independently checked records using the same validator. A lead is not evidence: a record must identify the exact title, edition and platform, with at least three submissions for each included play style.

`checkedAt`, `snapshotAt`, `dataSource` and `license` retain provenance for curators and distribution. They are not labels on game pages. Attribute the published datasets in distribution notices as described in `licenses/game-metadata.txt`. Refreshes must use datasets whose distribution terms permit this use; a research-only dataset is not a substitute for the licensed sources. The tooling stages changes by default, applies only with `--apply`, and never publishes. Do not create another catalogue feed or generation.
